newsitem.title: USA: Cablevision sees expansion with Garden buy.
newsitem.headline: Cablevision sees expansion with Garden buy.

text.p: Cablevision Systems Corp said Friday that its planned acquisition of Madison Square Garden will link sporting and entertainment events with technological advances to offer more choices to television viewers.

"We think the subscriber is entitled to see any game that's played. How we do that, whether it's on broadcast (television) or basic, premium, or Pay-Per-View (cable television) - it should be in some orderly fashion that's fair to the subscriber and yet provides the support the teams need to be attractive," said Cablevision chairman Charles Dolan.

Cablevision announced late Thursday that it would buy ITT Corp's 50 percent stake in the famed properties that include the arena -- the New York Knicks basketball team, the New York Rangers hockey team and the Madison Square Garden television network. The companies teamed up in 1995 to buy the Garden for $1 billion, with each holding a 50 percent stake.

The deal comes as ITT faces pressure following a $6.5 billion hostile takeover bid from Hilton Hotels Corp. The company is selling non-core assets to focus on its Sheraton hotels and Caesars casino businesses.
Dolan discussed the planned acquisition at a crowded news conference in Madison Square Garden that also featured ITT Corp chairman Rand Araskog and New York Governor George Pataki.

Dolan was not specific about plans to link Cablevision's services or pricing strategies. Cablevision also owns cable networks such as American Movie Classics and the SportsChannel Regional Network, which are offered on its systems and through other television service providers.
But he said that Madison Square Garden will serve a crucial role for expansion.

"Not only is it the Garden, but it is a wonderful distribution network outside of the Garden, which expands our box office capability and gives everybody a chance to participate in an event whether they want to take a train (to the Madison Square Garden site) or stay home and watch it on their wonderful new digital television," Dolan said.

Cablevision had been considered the most likely buyer of the ITT stake, although other parties expressed interest, the companies said. Dolan and Araskog downplayed a recent dispute over Cablevision's rights to acquire ITT's stake, but admitted their negotiations were adversarial.
Dolan said he hopes the transaction will be finalized by June 1, but admitted that regulatory and other required approvals could potentially delay the process.
Meanwhile, ITT officials took a low profile at the press conference, declining to discuss the Hilton takeover bid or plans for the proceeds from Madison Square Garden sale.
"I think the thing people should concentrate on is the value. For our shareholders, this was a wonderful transaction," Araskog said.
Dolan continued speaking with reporters after the news conference, while Araskog was whisked away from the area by ITT officials.
